title: Subsets: Choose, Explore, Undo
contract: Return every subset of distinct input integers. Sort the textual subsets for a deterministic output; input length ≤ 15 for interactive examples.
brute: List<String> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int mask=0;mask<(1<<a.length);mask++){List<Integer> subset=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++)if((mask&(1<<i))!=0)subset.add(a[i]);out.add(subset.toString());emit("Decode one subset mask","mask",mask,"subset",subset);}Collections.sort(out);return out;
reasoning: Enumerating masks is a direct exhaustive baseline with one inclusion bit per value.
Backtracking maintains a path, recursively includes or excludes a value, and undoes the inclusion before returning.

There are 2ⁿ outputs, so no algorithm can avoid exponential output work. Both methods are output-sensitive; the comparison illustrates control flow, not a false polynomial optimization. Final textual sorting adds O(2ⁿ log(2ⁿ)) comparisons.
complexity: O(n²2ⁿ) upper bound including output sorting, O(n2ⁿ)
O(n²2ⁿ) upper bound including output sorting, O(n) recursion excluding output
